Protectins, resolvins and maresins
211


Protectins
Independently of the neuroprotective action of protectin D1 mentioned above (Fig. 5), protectins decrease the secretion of
interferon-gamma (IFN-g), as well as tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-a), by blocking T-cell migration. Several studies have found
a new pathway of protectin synthesis, known as protectin D1, mediated by aspirin (Serhan et al., 2015b; Hamidzadeh et al., 2022).
In this new pathway, the synthesis of protectins is produced from DHA by the action of COX; this compound presents positive inter-
actions with receptors of the peroxisome proliferative receptor-gamma (PPAR-g) family. Both protectins, regardless of the synthesis
pathway by which they are obtained, decrease neutrophil transmigration through endothelial cells and enhance the efferocytosis
process (from the Latin effere, “to bring to the grave”) performed by macrophages for the elimination of apoptotic neutrophils.
